title: Social Work
tagline: Case managers, clinical social workers, and advocates — supporting people through systems.
summary: A deep-dive specialization of the Psychology & Counseling roadmap: social work from BSW through MSW and LCSW — case management, child and family services, clinical therapy, and macro practice.

sources.label: O*NET — Child, Family, and School Social Workers (21-1021.00)

detail.description: Social work connects people to resources and helps them through crises and systems — from child welfare and hospitals to therapy practices and policy, under a professional code of ethics.
detail.why: It is the most flexible mental-health degree: the LCSW license enables therapy, while the broader field spans case management to community leadership.
learn: Read the BLS OOH social workers profile
Learn micro, mezzo, and macro practice distinctions
Read the NASW Code of Ethics overview
Talk to one social worker per setting

resources.title: O*NET — Child, Family, and School Social Workers

detail.description: The Bachelor of Social Work (CSWE-accredited) includes supervised field practicum hours and qualifies graduates for generalist case-management roles — and advanced-standing MSW admission.
detail.why: A BSW is the fastest accredited entry into professional social work — and shortens the MSW later.
learn: Verify CSWE accreditation for programs
Compare field-practicum structures
Use the BSW to work while planning the MSW
Check advanced-standing MSW eligibility

detail.description: The core craft: assessment, service planning, connecting clients to benefits and providers, monitoring progress, and documenting everything defensibly.
detail.why: Case management is the field's largest job family — and the skill every other role builds on.
learn: Learn the assessment → plan → link → monitor cycle
Master documentation standards early
Build a local resource directory from scratch
Practice boundaries with high-need clients

resources.title: O*NET — Social and Human Service Assistants

detail.description: Social workers specialize by population: child and family (including child welfare), aging, medical/hospital, schools, addiction, and corrections — each with distinct systems.
detail.why: Population choice shapes licensure needs, emotional load, and daily work — sample before you commit.
learn: Volunteer or intern in two different populations
Learn each system's legal framework briefly
Note the emotional demands per setting
Pick a primary population to start

detail.description: The NASW Code of Ethics governs the profession: self-determination, confidentiality, dual relationships, cultural competence, and mandated-reporting duties.
detail.why: Social workers hold power over vulnerable people — ethics is the license's spine and the exam's core.
learn: Study the NASW Code section by section
Practice applying self-determination to real dilemmas
Learn dual-relationship rules for small communities
Know your state's reporting laws exactly

detail.description: The Master of Social Work (CSWE-accredited, ~2 years) offers clinical and macro concentrations with substantial internship hours; BSW holders qualify for advanced-standing one-year programs.
detail.why: The MSW is the gateway to clinical licensure (LCSW) and to supervisory and program-leadership roles.
learn: Verify CSWE accreditation before applying
Choose clinical vs macro concentration deliberately
Compare advanced-standing options for BSW holders
Plan internship hours around work

detail.description: Clinical social workers provide therapy (toward LCSW); macro social workers run programs, organize communities, and shape policy — both are 'real' social work.
detail.why: MSW programs force this fork — choosing it consciously prevents mid-degree regret.
learn: Shadow one clinical and one macro social worker
Compare daily outputs: therapy notes vs program reports
Assess which change scale energizes you
Confirm your concentration supports licensure if wanted

detail.description: Child-protective work: investigations, safety assessment, family reunification services, court documentation, and foster-care coordination — demanding and consequential.
detail.why: Child welfare is the largest social-work employer and a profound responsibility — many agencies fund MSWs for committed staff.
learn: Learn your state's child-welfare structure
Practice objective safety documentation
Understand court timelines and roles
Build resilience habits before, not after

resources.title: O*NET — Child, Family, and School Social Workers

tasks: Assess family and social situations, provide counseling, arrange services, and maintain case records for children and families.

detail.description: Hospital social workers handle discharge planning, crisis intervention, resource connection, and family support inside clinical teams.
detail.why: Medical social work is salaried, structured, and teaches rapid assessment — a strong MSW internship target.
learn: Learn discharge-planning workflows
Practice crisis conversations with families
Coordinate with nursing and case-management teams
Learn insurance-driven care constraints

detail.description: Licensed clinical social workers deliver psychotherapy independently after the MSW, supervised clinical hours, and the ASWB clinical exam — the profession's therapy license.
detail.why: LCSW combines therapy practice with systems training — the most portable mental-health license.
learn: Confirm your state's LCSW hour requirements
Complete supervised clinical hours with quality supervision
Pass the ASWB clinical exam
Choose post-licensure training in a therapy modality

certs.name: LCSW
certs.note: Licensed Clinical Social Worker — MSW plus supervised clinical experience plus the ASWB clinical exam.

detail.description: Macro practice runs programs and changes systems: nonprofit leadership, community organizing, grant management, and policy advocacy for the populations social workers serve.
detail.why: Macro social work scales impact beyond one client at a time — leadership without leaving the mission.
learn: Learn community-organizing frameworks
Practice grant-writing for a local nonprofit
Follow state policy affecting your population
Join a coalition or board as a beginner

resources.title: BLS OOH — Social and Community Service Managers

detail.description: Social work documentation is legal and clinical: objective language, defensible decisions, timelines, and privacy — often reviewed in courts and audits.
detail.why: Files protect clients and workers alike — documentation quality is a hiring and survival skill.
learn: Practice objective, non-judgmental note style
Learn your agency's format (DAP/SOAP variants)
Keep timelines exact for court settings
Audit your own files monthly

detail.description: Ladders: case manager → supervisor → program director → agency executive; clinical: associate → LCSW → supervisor/private practice; macro: organizer → program manager → policy roles.
detail.why: Social work ladders fork at the MSW — knowing your fork early shapes concentrations and hours.
learn: Map the ladder for your chosen fork
Identify licensure/credential needs per rung
Find a mentor who took your path
Set a 5-year goal with annual reviews

detail.description: Social workers absorb others' crises daily — vicarious trauma, burnout, and secondary stress are occupational realities with evidence-based counters.
detail.why: The field's turnover problem is preventable with supervision, boundaries, and real self-care — starting in school.
learn: Learn vicarious-trauma signs and counters
Use supervision to process hard cases
Keep caseloads honest — advocate for limits
Maintain life outside the work deliberately

detail.description: Social work licensure is state-specific with varying titles and requirements; the ASWB Passport-style mobility options and endorsement processes matter for movers.
detail.why: License portability affects every relocation — checking rules before moving prevents career gaps.
learn: Compare license titles and tiers across states you'd consider
Learn the endorsement process
Track CE requirements per state held
Note telehealth practice rules across lines

detail.description: LCSWs deliver therapy by video widely — with platform privacy rules, emergency protocols at a distance, and multistate practice considerations.
detail.why: Telehealth made social-work therapy careers location-flexible — with new professional duties to master.
learn: Learn telehealth privacy and platform standards
Practice remote rapport-building techniques
Build distance emergency protocols
Check interstate practice rules for your clients
